fact: CAMTEL said at the SAGO conference of 9 June 2026 that its Zamengoe Data Centre is a critical national asset ensuring the security, continuity and local control of government data; the document does not list the specific systems hosted.

Le Jour reports that the state, through Camtel, is building the Tier III Zamengoe data centre as a tool for a sovereign digital ecosystem, with the aim of producing and preserving data generated on national territory, as presented by Camtel director general Judith Yah Sunday at SAGO 2026.
CAMTEL's press release says its agreement with Ethio Telecom, signed 4 December 2025, covers establishing a sovereign Government Cloud to support digitalising public services.
Camtel says its Zamengoé data centre guarantees local hosting of sensitive national data, and that more than a hundred public and private administrations host their data there.

Key government ministries and state administrations host their data at Camtel's Zamengoue Data Center in Cameroon, which also hosts the call centres of numerous state administrations, per Camtel's General Manager as reported by News Upfront.

The webinar record says Cameroon's universal health coverage (openIMIS) data is hosted at CAMTEL's national data centre in the country, chosen for digital sovereignty, with MINSANTE governing data and access.
